chapter: Kirby again, Garland gigs and later recordings
title: Garland's death and the end of his playing
summary: Joe and Moses Garland died a day apart, ending the gigs; Holmes stopped playing after a foot operation and loss of sight in one eye.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: When Joe Garland died, I guess those gigs stopped.
Oh, that was the end of it, yeah. Well...
His brother died one day, and he died the next! The two of them were gone. That's it. That was it. Yes, both of them died of the same thing within one day of each other.
And at that point you decided more or less to pack up and put your horn away?

No. No, I didn't put my horn away until... Well, I guess I was sick then. When I got sick, when I got sick... I mean, this foot... And they operated on me, and I couldn't get around any more, and I'd lost sight in my
eye... But when I got so I couldn't get around, couldn't stand up, that was it, as far as I was concerned.
